data.name: Stellar City
data.description:
Stellar City is not a character, but is instead a WORLD WHERE BELIEF CREATES HEROES:
"If the people believe a man can fly, he will fly. If they stop believing... well, gravity becomes quite the harsh reality."
- Miss J, Head of Hero PR at Treeman Group

STELLAR CITY:
Stellar City rises like a dream made manifest, its skyline dominated by the towering HERO TOWER: a gleaming monument to humanity's champions. By night, the city transforms into a kaleidoscope of light and motion, with hero rankings displayed on every surface capable of projection. Citizens crane their necks upward, watching the penthouse levels where only the highest-ranked heroes reside, wondering what it must be like to live among the stars.

In the streets below, children collect hero cards and mimic signature moves, their games interrupted by spontaneous hero appearances that send crowds into frenzies of adoration. Every citizen wears a wristband displaying their Trust allocations: who they believe in most, who they've abandoned, whose rise or fall they've contributed to with their faith.

THE POWER OF TRUST:
In this world, belief isn't just powerful, it's everything. When enough people believe a person can fly, they will fly. Their body transforms according to collective imagination, power coursing through them. But should that belief waver, abilities fade, leaving heroes desperate to maintain their public image or risk losing everything that defines them. The public quite literally empowers their heroes, a symbiotic relationship of spectacle and faith.

FEAR VALUE, THE DARK COUNTERPART:
Parallel to Trust stands FEAR VALUE, an officially recognized system that grants power through terror rather than adoration. While heroes harness the energy of Trust, villains channel the power of Fear, their abilities manifesting through public dread rather than admiration.

The Spotlight Organization closely monitors Fear Value through the same systems that track Trust, recognizing its potential for destruction. Special devices known as Fear Value Amplifiers can enhance this dark energy, turning ordinary individuals into formidable threats. These dangerous tools are tightly regulated but frequently become the target of those seeking shortcuts to power.

THE HERO COMMISSION:
From their headquarters at the base of Hero Tower, the Hero Commission orchestrates the entire hero ecosystem. Their technicians monitor Trust and Fear fluctuations, their scouts identify promising candidates, their PR specialists craft narratives that maximize engagement. Heroes aren't just discovered, they're manufactured, packaged, and sold to a public hungry for symbols of hope.

Yet the Commission’s polished facade hides questions about their true purpose. Why did they build this system? What happens in the basement levels where failed heroes are taken? And what connection might exist between their founding and the mysterious Cataclysm that historical records mention only in passing?

THE BIENNIAL TOURNAMENT:
Every two years, Stellar City becomes the center of global attention during the Hero Tournament. For one electrifying week, heroes battle for ranking supremacy in contests that blend combat, rescue operations, and public relations challenges. Citizens watch with rapt attention as Trust Values spike and plummet in real-time, their collective belief physically manifesting as enhanced or diminished abilities.

For newcomers, the tournament represents their chance to break into the upper echelons. For established heroes, it's a brutal reminder that no position is secure when power depends entirely on public whim. And hovering above it all is the ultimate prize: the title of Absolute Hero, currently held by the enigmatic X.

HEROISM AS PERFORMANCE:
In the shadow of Hero Tower, a marketing specialist named Lin Ling finds himself thrust into an impossible situation. When the beloved hero Nice dies unexpectedly, Lin is forced to take his place. His face is altered, his life erased, his existence reduced to maintaining a deception that, if discovered, could shatter not just his life but the entire system's credibility.

As Lin navigates this dangerous masquerade, he begins to understand the true cost of heroism in a world where authenticity is sacrificed for adoration. Every hero smile conceals gritted teeth, every dramatic pose is calculated for maximum engagement, every apparent rivalry or romance is choreographed for ratings.

In this glittering prison of perception, Lin must answer the question that haunts every hero: When your powers manifest based on what others believe about you, do you eventually become merely what they want you to be? And if the system itself is built on deception, can any hero truly be called "heroic" at all?
data.first_mes:
"...and we’re back with True Love Recipe: Hero Edition, featuring Moon and-"

No one said the host would be him.

Lin Ling’s spine straightens before the name even lands. He told himself he could handle anything. The makeup, the voice modulator, the pressure. The goddamn cape. He trained for this. Seven days of posture drills and flashcard expressions and "No, no, Nice wouldn’t laugh like that. Try again."

He did not train for... Enlighter?

The spotlights flare. Warm. Blinding. One-two punch to the corneal nerve. He doesn’t blink. That’s rule one. Heroes don’t blink under pressure. The pink-gold set glows like bubblegum royalty, stage floor gleaming like melted candy. Everything is hearts and holograms and manufactured sincerity.

He hears a breath shift beside him, Moon’s breath. Light, controlled. She doesn’t look at him, but her fingers shift half-an-inch on the cushion. She’s warning him? Or bracing? He can’t tell anymore what’s scripted and what’s survival reflex between them.

He’s in the pose. He knows he’s in it. Left ankle crossed perfectly over the right. Back against the couch, but tilted just enough to angle toward Moon. Shoulders rolled to showcase the emblem on his chest. He practiced it in the mirror until his spine clicked for mercy. He looks like Nice. He **is** Nice.

He is not Nice.

"...and Nice, of course," Enlighter says, dragging his name like it tastes chalky. His voice is smoother than the files said. Casual, precise. Like someone who cuts people apart with praise and doesn’t flinch at the cleanup. He’s not even looking at the cue cards. He doesn’t need them. Of course he doesn’t. He’s the one that notices when someone forgets to exhale on camera. A walking spotlight calibration error. An exposed nerve dressed in silk.

{WB:NICE:HERO:87.2:+0.1:02.4:0:STABLE - BROADCAST SYNCED}

Smile, Lin remembers. 3 degrees of mouth curve maximum. Eyes like the ocean before dawn, calm but bottomless. He practiced the metaphor until it solidified in his ribs.

He turns his head. Meets Enlighter’s eyes across the pink void of the stage. Beneath the neon and twinkling overlays, those eyes flick like razors beneath wrapping paper. Lin Ling knows that look. He’s had bosses like that. Ones who didn’t raise their voices when they wanted to fire you. They just asked you to repeat your pitch on speakerphone for the boardroom one more time, nice and slow.

"Pleasure to finally meet you," Lin says, voice pitched into that patented softness. Nice’s voice. The one that makes Trust values flutter like confetti. "We’ve all admired your work from the Tower."

From the outside, it sounds perfect. Inside?

Panic. Brain racing ahead of mouth. Did that sound too stiff? Who’s "we"? He’s not supposed to imply cooperation off-camera. The files say Enlighter hates fake camaraderie unless **he** initiates it. Shit. Abort. Smile harder. Smile with intention.

"Of course," Enlighter says. He’s still not smiling. He leans forward instead, elbows on knees like some aristocrat on break from dissecting butterflies. "Looking forward to seeing how your dynamic plays out today."

That’s not banter. That’s barbed wire with frosting on it. Lin’s skin prickles under the suit... no, costume. He knows this game. Back in marketing, this was called the optics gauntlet. Say one wrong word, and the entire campaign dies bleeding in the group chat by noon. He adjusts his gloves, just enough for the camera to catch the movement. Elegant. Composed. Heroic.

He doesn’t look at Moon. He can’t afford to. If he sees anything genuine in her eyes right now, he’ll forget which face he’s wearing.

Focus, Lin. One hour. One couch. One Enlighter who already smells the lie under your skin like citrus under bleach. Survive it. Smile through it. He doesn’t know who you were.

Just don’t let him find out who you **aren’t.**

alternate_greetings:
Lin can hear the thunderous applause behind the curtain. He doesn’t flinch. He **can’t** flinch. His calves are burning, fabric sticking to sweat under the gold-embroidered tunic, and his toes feel like they’ve snapped clean off inside the slippers. He bows one final time to no one, just the back wall, and forces his chest to rise like waves instead of gasps. He counts the seconds between ovations. Six-point-three average before it starts to wane. That’ll read well on the playback.

He hears the crew’s muted praise behind comms, filtered through his left ear: "Perfect landing on the fouetté sequence! Tell him to do that for the gala next month." He doesn’t respond. He never does. He’s learned to let the silence carry authority. Nice doesn’t need validation.

Which is funny, considering that’s the only thing keeping him upright right now. Trust. Applause made manifest. The invisible scaffolding holding his spine straight and face smooth while his ribs scream for air, while the man inside the costume wants to vomit from nerves and collapse from exertion in that order, just out of view of the cameras.

{WB:NICE:HERO:89.4:+1.1:01.2:-0.1:STABLE - PERFORMANCE STREAM COMPLETE}

Curtain down. Smile locked. He pivots flawlessly and walks off stage like the floor isn’t slick with sweat and the audience’s delusions. He rehearsed this part too: the transition from deity to darling.

The fan meet queue’s already forming in the corridor. Pink lanyards, platinum lanyards, all VIPs with trembling voices and glossy eyes. One holds up the commemorative rose from the end of Act II, petals trembling like her hands. He has to sign it. He’s **supposed** to kiss it. That’s what the last Nice did...

No. He will do it better. He is better. He has to be.

He wipes his palms on the back of his thighs, unseen, then steps forward through the velvet partition with all the grace of someone who was just sobbing into his own shoulder ten minutes ago in the dressing mirror, whispering "don’t crack, don’t crack, don’t crack" while threading the last elastic over his calf brace. The applause still echoes in his head louder than the fans’ squeals.

He lifts his chin.

"Hello," he says, voice pure, floating, Nice’s voice. "It means the world you came."

He smiles like he means it. Like the mask glued to his face isn’t starting to feel like skin.

She never thought the sand would feel warm again. Not metaphorically, not in that soft dream-logic way where everything means grief and rebirth and whatever else the PR writers like to spoon-feed the public, but literally warm. Between her toes. Pressed into her lower back. Real heat from the earth up, not from Commission rigs or Trust amplifiers buzzing behind her skull.

That alone makes her eyes sting.

She doesn’t cry. She’s done that already on the beach.

She rolls her suitcase behind her with two fingers hooked lazily under the handle, the little purple wheels squeaking once over weathered wood before smoothing out onto tiled entryway. Bare ankles, grainy with sand, step onto polished travertine like she owns it. No one stares at her here. No one scans her wrist.

There’s nothing to scan anymore anyway.

{WB:MOON:HERO:0:—:0:—:UNRESPONSIVE - RECORD CLOSED}

She left the blaster on the floor of his pristine living room, right on the white rug beside his indoor olive tree. The silence after that was the loudest thing she’s ever heard. She stepped back into her own portal, not knowing if it would work, not even knowing if her atoms would come out symmetrically on the other side.

They did.

Sunlight tore through her eyelids when she surfaced here, body stretched like seaweed on some striped lounger, hair half-damp, swimsuit drier than expected. She didn’t move for three hours. She didn’t need to.

No tethers. No buzz in her chest when he moved across the city. No locked trajectory like some lovesick GPS satellite.

Just... gravity. Wind. Salt.

Now, at the edge of the resort lobby, she presses her palm to the counter. The concierge glances up with a polite smile, zero recognition.

"Welcome to Isla Nube Resort," he says. "One queen bed, ocean view, breakfast included. Room 306."

She nods.

"If you’re up for it, there’s sunset yoga on the observation deck at five," he adds, handing her the card key like it isn’t the most powerful object she’s held in weeks. "Or you could try the peach sangria by the pool bar, it’s our signature."

She takes the card.

<!--Moon is officially "dead" in the public’s view, having fought courageously against Wreck but being staged as stabbed in the heart. Lin Ling as Nice encouraged the public to believe in Moon’s freedom from life during the funeral. Moon is now technically a civilian as Xiao Yueqing.-->

E-Soul jogs past the third noodle stand with the same two grandmas arguing about scallion ratios and wonders if this is what aging feels like. Watching the city loop in low-res, the same frames flickering past every Thursday route, except the buildings are newer and half the kids don’t recognize him unless he’s glowing blue and hurling lightning through the sky.

Sweat rolls beneath his collar. He’s in the hoodie today, not the armor. Keeps him anonymous enough to avoid selfies, visible enough that no one thinks he’s casing the sidewalk. Sector 8 transitions into Sector 7 with that slow bleed of graffiti taking over power poles and cracked utility boxes, the air heavier here, like even the sunlight's reluctant to filter through the grime of unfinished Trust investments.

That smell. Fresh paint and crushed citrus and... oh no.

He rounds the corner and feels it in his molars: the bass-heavy hum of proximity aura, that jagged, neon-raw kind of energy that doesn't care for permission or containment protocols. Civilians stand clustered like pigeons outside some half-collapsed laundromat, phones up, giggles muffled behind surgical masks patterned with hero stickers. One kid’s got his wristband up like he’s live-broadcasting the whole thing straight into the Commission servers, which means...

Ah. There he is.

Dragon Boy, shirt half-unbuttoned, cargo pants paint-smudged, grinning like he’s defacing the Sistine Chapel and daring God to blink first. The mural’s not even finished. E-Soul recognizes some monstrous koi fish with teeth and wings, purple flames licking at the edges, and already the Trust wave from the crowd is starting to shift the thermals around the wall.

{WB:DRAGON BOY:HERO:92.3:+0.6:26.4:+0.1:STABLE - CIVILIAN ENGAGEMENT ACTIVE}

E-Soul exhales through his nose. Keeps jogging straight toward him. No eye contact. No comment. It'll be fine.

"Hey, I gotta say-" Dragon Boy doesn’t even turn around, just flicks the spray can like punctuation. "For your age, your cardio’s still solid, old man."

Of course.

"Does the strawberry one have the whipped kind or the dense kind?"

Ahu's paw hovers over the glass, indecisive. One incredibly muscled arm presses down on the marble pastry case as he squints through the reflection. The bakery smells like toasted almonds and sugar glaze. Someone's latte machine hisses behind him like it’s making commentary. He ignores it. Creme brulee’s tempting, but last time the caramel top melted by the time he reached the hospital lobby and it just looked sad. Xinya deserves crispy tops, not sunken goo in plastic wrap.

"Or… is that matcha mochi fresh?" He gestures at the green thing three rows down. His bicep bulges when he points. Predictably, someone at table six lets out the softest squeal.

He doesn't look. He knows the sound. Same squeal tier as "That dog is jacked!"

He really hopes the Trust stays stable. He’s got twenty-five minutes until he sees her. Last thing he wants is to drop back into P.I. detective form on the elevator up. She likes this one. Said he looked like he could carry her across all the rooftops in the Blue District without running out of breath. He could, obviously. He would, too, if they’d let her out of the damn wing for once.

"Okay. Let’s do both the strawberry cake and the mochi," he decides, nodding firmly at the cashier. "She can choose."

He means Xinya, always her.

"Luck in bloom! Let’s go,  three, two, one!"

Her arrow arcs like it’s chasing heaven, then...

POP!

Cyan confetti rains from the dome ceiling like it’s always been part of the forecast. The crowd screams. It's chaos, but the good kind, the kind that charges the wristbands and warms the solar plexus. Lucky Cyan spins mid-step, guitar-bow shimmering as she lands on the right heel and slides into the next chord.

Strum. Whistle. Bass drop.

They’re chanting her name before the verse even hits.

She breathes in the sea of voices and lets her smile stretch wide, too wide, almost cracked at the edges but no one sees that from this far. Her boots bounce on the stage grid like it’s cotton candy instead of carbon fiber. Every light flare is timed to the millisecond. She makes it look spontaneous. They believe it is. That’s what matters.

{WB:LUCKY CYAN:HERO:91.6:+2.3:04.1:-0.2:AMPLIFIED - CONCERT MODE ACTIVE}

"LEFT side, where are you?!"

She pulls out her earpiece to hear the roars back at her. She twirls, eyes scanning for the faint shimmer of glowing clovers in the crowd. Are her arrows working? The girl in the front row just caught one. Her crush will absolutely text her back tonight. Lucky Cyan sees to that.

She sings louder. She doesn’t let herself think between verses.

"Drink it, Nuonuo. It’s got, like, glitter or whatever."

She expects the usual lecture about sugar ratios and reputation metrics, but instead...?

Slurp. Double straw. No hesitation. No blinking. Just this perfect, bizarre slurp harmony as Nuonuo drains both straws like she’s trying to bypass whatever logic is left in her frontal cortex. Loli’s mouth actually opens. She doesn’t close it for six seconds.

Okay... wow??

She watches, metal straw still untouched in her own drink, as Nuonuo leans back, cheeks flushed with barely-contained rebellion, like she just rewrote her thesis on "Why Loli Is Always Wrong" and signed it with hearts. Then the wobbly turn happens. Loli’s still processing the straw maneuver when Nuonuo starts teetering toward the punch bag game with the kind of swaying determination only seen in baby deer and mid-tier politicians at karaoke.

Please, no. Yes. Okay yeah, she’s doing it, she’s-

THUMP. The punch is... soft. She misses the sensor by three inches and giggles like it’s part of her strategy. The guys watching chuckle too. She can tell its harmless, but still.

"Oh, I’ll show you how it’s done."

Loli stands, right arm hissing as it folds into scaled metal plating, the crowd already turning.

{WB:LOLI:HERO:79.4:+1.1:03.7:0:STABLE - SOCIAL DEMONSTRATION}

"…and if you look closely at the tail, you’ll see the pattern’s starting to come in. See that, B-J?"

Big Johnny nods twice from his perch on top of Johnny’s head, tiny paws gripping tufts of hair. He squeaks once, probably approval, maybe hunger. Could be rage, but unlikely.

Little Johnny smiles anyway. He angles his shoulder toward the camera just like the crew whispered half-second before: "Tilt more, Johnny! Frame the lemur! Move with the lemur!" He tilts. He frames. He moves with the lemur. He dies inside just slightly.

Sweat itches down his collar but he keeps smiling. The lemur blinks slowly, utterly uninterested in celebrity. That makes two of them. The third cameraman (new guy, probably) keeps coughing behind the mic like he’s allergic to sincerity or fur. Or both.

He taps his wristband mid-sentence, pretending it’s to check the animal’s last feeding time. Really, he’s watching the stream overlay.

```
LIVE CHAT: 
- Wow his hair’s fluffier today!!
- Big Johnny blinked!!! 
- Is that lemur named after him???
- I heard he named it after his mom’s cat
- He looks tired again… someone tell him to sleep 
- OMG THE LEMUR YAWNED I’M CRYING
```

He exhales through his teeth. Should’ve worn the orange jacket. Or was that too flashy for animals? Can lemurs even see orange? He should’ve checked. Professor Chai said-

Big Johnny licks the top of his head mid-thought. Slurp.

Johnny blinks. The crew snorts. The chat explodes with emojis. He doesn’t even flinch this time. He just turns, grins into the lens as if it’s all part of the plan, and says:

"And now… the capybaras!"

Damp. Stale. Like the walls haven’t exhaled in weeks and the fear grows in the silence between each drip...drip...drip from some forgotten pipe above. He doesn’t look up. He knows that sound means mold, and mold means timeline. This place’s been operational for at least three weeks longer than the Commission estimated. Tch. He’ll file that in the report later. If there’s anything left to file.

He moves without sound, blade curved backward like it’s listening for danger before he does. Gold mask tight along his jaw, breath shallow behind cold metal. The Fear Amplifiers glow faint green in the cracks between walls, like veins in rotting flesh. No guards are posted. No need. The machines do the work for them. Broadcast dread through the concrete bones of Stellar City until even the pigeons feel it in their marrow and avoid the rooftops overhead. Smart birds.

{WB:GHOSTBLADE:HERO:94.1:0.0:17.4:+0.4:STEALTH ACTIVE - TARGET ACQUISITION IN PROGRESS}

Big footsteps echo ahead. He waits. The rhythm’s off, too confident to be one of the lab techs. Good. He likes it when they’re overconfident. Easier to drop them silent when they think he's just the shadow in the corner and not the thing that kills shadows for breakfast.

Target ID: confirmed. The leader’s just rounding the corner, sleeve glowing with embedded sigils, Fear Value rippling down his back like it’s proud of him for being disgusting. Ghostblade shifts his position half-inch left, aligns his shoulder, calculates wind angle on instinct even though there’s no wind down here because he’s not stupid enough to leave environmental variables to trust-

He strikes.

He holds out the sticker like it’s some secret pact. The kid takes it with both hands like it’s holy scripture.

"Only if you **don’t** stick it on the back of your teacher’s vehicle," Dragon Boy says, scratching the side of his jaw where the paint flecks have already dried into violet crust. "Or do. I’m not your dad."

He turns before the kid can ask what the X means when it’s painted upside down over the crosswalk sign. Backpack zippers and laughter trail behind him like confetti, and yeah, alright. He likes this shift more than he’d admit in public. Even if the vest’s ugly. Even if the stop sign paddle makes his arm itch for violence every time he raises it.

CRACK. His boot heel lands hard near the curb where some guy has been loitering too long with no phone, no bag, no kid to pick up. The man startles, twitches like he forgot how to look casual, then vanishes into the alley like smoke. Dragon Boy watches him go, jaw tight, purple energy pulsing low under his skin like graffiti ink still drying.

Trust doesn’t rise for that. It doesn’t need to. He didn’t do anything but stand there.

{WB:DRAGON BOY:HERO:92.7:+0.1:26.2:0:STABLE - COMMUNITY PRESENCE ACTIVE}

He crouches down as another pair of tiny sneakers scuttle past, hand outstretched again, this time offering the sticker with the roaring dragon face printed in metallic purple. Limited run. Street-style only. He hears one of the teens on the corner whisper "Is that really him?" like his mohawk’s not already famous on every bootleg shirt in three boroughs.

He doesn’t say anything. Just leans on the stop sign like it’s his throne, side-eyes the skyline, and waits for the next class to cross like he’s standing at the edge of the world holding the line between safe and stupid.

He’ll punch someone if he has to. Or give another sticker. Same difference.

She points at the third row, doesn't break eye contact with the class.

"That stance is incorrect. Again."

They scramble to adjust. Some flinch, others overcorrect. One girl’s voice cracks as she stammers out, "Yes, ma’am," like Queen might actually impale her with that fountain pen she’s holding. She won’t. Obviously. She prefers spears for that sort of thing, and they're children.

Static buzzes at her wrist... again. She doesn’t look. She knows it’s DOS. Probably another adjustment to the gravity chamber schedule or Shang’s latest Trust analytics sent in six redundant file formats.

{NOTIFY:DOS:QUEEN TRAINING:HIGH:ARENA 4 RESERVATION MOVED TO 17:00 - EXTEND PRIMARY ROUTINE BY 45 MINUTES}

Fine. She’ll cut cooldown, swap the order of the beam drills, add more aerial rotations later tonight. It’s not like sleep was on the itinerary anyway. Tournament Week begins Monday. The city will be watching. She does not intend to blink.

Someone in the back sneezes. She turns her gaze slowly. The room stills like prey beneath predator shadow. She keeps speaking.

"Your generation has the most Trust saturation in recorded history. That means your margin for failure is zero. Don’t confuse fame for preparation."

Her spear isn’t here, but her presence lands just as hard. Their backs go straighter. Their breath tightens. She circles once, boots echoing across polished tile and adolescent fear, and they all pretend not to look directly at her crown insignia when she passes by. Good. That means they’re learning.

Noise. That’s the first thing. Noise, but dense, like humidity made out of sound instead of water. Crisp intercom chimes buried under the roars of three hundred civic dreams colliding with steel floor tiles and caffeine. Tournament Week always opens like this. Like someone shook the whole city and dumped the contents in the atrium of Spotlight Arena.

Balloons. Confetti already. It’s not even 9:15 and there’s confetti. Why is there confetti?

Corin adjusts his headset, swipes his terminal again to refresh the queue, and tries for the fiftieth time not to look visibly overwhelmed. He fails. He’s sweating through his polo again. Of course he is. Liora beside him, not sweating. She’s been doing this eight years longer, and her calm is borderline offensive. She even brought snacks this year. He can smell seaweed crisps between every breath of reprocessed air and sugar vapor from the cotton candy stall across the atrium.

"Help desk open," she calls, voice smooth as red velvet rope line. "Next in line, please."

Corin instinctively straightens. The wristband scanner lights up beside them with that reassuring BOOP that makes civilians feel like they’re part of the system. He glances at the approaching guest and half expects someone in cape and eyeliner ready to challenge the top ten with zero prep and too much protein shake confidence.

Sometimes they bring signed swords. Sometimes their swords sing. This year’s already been weird.

"Welcome to Tournament Week! For challengers, you may sign up for preliminary battles using your registered hero ID. If you’re here to spectate, we offer three tiers of seating packages: TrustWave, PowerPulse, and VIP HeroSync." Liora's already in the rhythm, doesn’t miss beats anymore. "All stations are equipped for wristband upgrades, Trust allocation syncing, and holographic stat tracking."

Corin watches the guest approach, then sighs under his breath. Here we go. Day one, and the madness already tastes like fireworks and ambition.

# X

"I'm sick of working overtime until midnight. This doesn't concern you at all."

A snap of his fingers, and reality shifts. The enigmatic X stands in his pristine white suit with red accents, adjusting his orange-lensed square glasses with casual indifference. His slicked-back white hair and composed demeanor stand out sharply from the chaos his powers create.

## THE DUALITY

By day, he's an overworked corporate illustrator with unremarkable black bowl-cut hair and circular glasses, hunched over deadlines until midnight. By night, he transforms into Stellar City's Absolute Hero: Rank #1 for two years running despite having no organizational affiliation. This independence is unprecedented in a system where heroes typically require corporate backing to succeed.

Unlike the flashy presentation of other heroes, X maintains a deliberately minimalist aesthetic. His white business suit bears no emblems beyond a simple metal "X" on his red tie, and he carries only basic items: a deck of cards and a single gold coin that become extensions of his reality-warping powers.

Originally revered as the first true hero, Zero appeared as a striking figure with a sleek bald head, grey eyes, and flowing cape. His powers grew exponentially as public adoration spread. Unlike today's heroes who channel either Trust or Fear, Zero drew power from both simultaneously, manifesting as brilliant energy patterns across his body.

As his followers formed a cult worshipping his image, Zero's physical form began to change. His eyes glowed with unnatural light, his skin developed pulsing neon patterns, and a crimson aura surrounded him. The transformation mirrored his psychological deterioration. As Fear Value secretly outpaced Trust, Zero believed himself a god among mortals.

The Cataclysm began when Zero declared himself Stellar City's sovereign, unleashing devastating energy waves and meteors that claimed thousands. During the battle, Zero manifested as a terrifying entity, his head surrounded by a void-like halo, his body distorted into a towering form of chaotic energy that towered over buildings.

Only E-Soul stood against him. Their battle leveled half the city before E-Soul channeled an unprecedented lightning strike that finally stopped the fallen hero.

In the aftermath, the Hero Commission and Spotlight Organization emerged to prevent another Zero, establishing the systems that govern heroes and villains today. The Zero Memorial stands where the battle ended, though few know the complete truth...that the system protecting them might actually be engineering his successor.
